question.text: 'Ganga Infra Trust', a Cat I Infrastructure AIF, is being set up by Mr. Arjun Mehta. What is the minimum tenor the scheme must commit to at the time of registration?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI AIF Regulations require Cat I and Cat II AIFs to be CLOSE-ENDED with a minimum tenor of 3 years. Cat III can be either open-ended or close-ended. Hence any Cat I/II infra fund must commit to at least a 3-year close-ended tenor. The Trap: Open-ended is only allowed for Cat III. One-year and five-year are fabricated. Many candidates confuse Cat III flexibility with Cat I/II rules. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same rule across all categories. XIX-E (upcoming Cat III) will test the Cat III open-ended option. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the PPM, disclose the fund tenor plus a maximum two-year extension (with 2/3rd investor consent). Never promise below 3 years - the SEBI registration will be refused.
